newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain CPI fall should see rate cuts - Montoro.
newsitem.headline: Spain CPI fall should see rate cuts - Montoro.

text.p: A continued improvement in inflation should see Spanish interest rates come down, Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said on Wednesday.

"This is a decision which corresponds to the Bank of Spain, so (the central bank) will choose the right moment" Montoro told national radio, "But to the extent that inflation continues to fall and the deficit continues to improve...interest rate cuts will emerge," he said.
Montoro reiterated that inflation will fall beneath two percent soon.
"This spring inflation will fall below two percent, this is what the Economy Ministry is expecting," he said.
April inflation data is due later this morning. The rate is forecast to fall to around 1.9 percent from 2.2 percent year on year in March.
Montoro also reiterated that Spain was one of the firmest candidates for entry into Europe's single currency, and will easily meet the Maastricht criteria for monetary union.
"We will enter monetary union in perfect social conditions, we won't arrive stretched, nor with our tongues hanging out; we'll arrive in perfect physical condition," he said.
